sanskrit: yad vo agnir ajahād ekam aṅgaṃ pitṛlokaṃ gamayaṃ jātavedāḥ | tad va etat punar ā veśayāmi sāṅgāḥ sarve pitaro mādayadhvam ||
english: Whatever single limb Agni Jātavedas took from you and conveyed to the world of the fathers — that same limb I now restore into you again. With all your limbs complete, O ancestors, all of you rejoice.

sanskrit: asau hā iha te manaḥ | kaputsalam iva jāmayo 'bhy enaṃ bhūma ūrṇūhi ||
english: There — here indeed is your mind. As kinswomen cluster around a kaputsala bird, O Earth, cover him over.

sanskrit: ramadhvaṃ mā bibhītanā asmin goṣṭhe karīṣiṇaḥ | ūrjaṃ dadhānāḥ sakṛtaḥ śacivratā gṛhā jīvanta upa vaḥ sadema ||
english: Take delight, do not be afraid, O dung-enriched ones, in this cattle-yard. Bearing vigor, single-dung-makers, of excellent vows — may we dwell beside you with these living houses.

sanskrit: ūrjaṃ me devā adadhur ūrjaṃ manuṣyā uta | ūrjaṃ pitṛbhya āhārṣam ūrjasvanto gṛhā mama ||
english: The gods have bestowed vigor upon me; humans too have bestowed vigor. I have brought vigor from the ancestors; may my houses be full of vigor.

sanskrit: payo me devā adadhuḥ payo manuṣyā uta | payaḥ pitṛbhya āharṣaṃ payasvanto gṛhā mama ||
english: The gods have bestowed milk upon me; humans too have bestowed milk. I have brought milk from the ancestors; may my houses be rich in milk.

sanskrit: ud uttamaṃ varuṇa pāśam asmad avādhamaṃ vi madhyamaṃ śrathāya | athāditya vrate vayaṃ tava- -anāgaso 'ditaye syāma ||
english: Loosen the highest fetter from us, O Varuṇa; loosen the lowest; unloose the middle one. Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless in your vow, and free for Aditi.

sanskrit: ye te śataṃ varuṇa ye sahasraṃ yajñiyāḥ pāśā vitatā mahāntaḥ | tebhyo asmān varuṇaḥ soma indro viśve muñcantu marutaḥ svarkāḥ ||
english: Those hundred bonds of yours, O Varuṇa, those thousand sacred and vast fetters stretched wide — from all of them may Varuṇa, Soma, Indra, all the Maruts, and the Svarkāḥ release us.

sanskrit: prāsmat pāśān varuṇa muñca sarvān yaiḥ samame badhyate yair vyāme | atha jīvema śaradaḥ śatāni tvāya rājan gupito rakṣamāṇaḥ ||
english: Release all fetters from us, O Varuṇa — those by which I am bound when lying on my side, those by which when stretched out. Then may we live a hundred autumns, protected and guarded, O king, as belonging to you.

sanskrit: ava te heḍa īmahe namobhir ava yajñebhir īmahe havirbhiḥ | (…)yad asmad varuṇa praceto rājann enāṃsi śiśrathaḥ kṛtāni ||
english: We implore the abatement of your wrath with obeisances; we implore it with sacrifices, with oblations. […] Whatever sins committed against us, O Varuṇa, O wise king, those you have loosened.

sanskrit: candramā apsv antar ā suparṇo dhāvate divi | na vo hiraṇyanemayaḥ padaṃ vindanti vidyuto vittaṃ me asya rodasī ||
english: The moon runs within the waters; the eagle runs through the sky. O lightnings, your golden-wheeled ones find no foothold. Know for me the two worlds of this one.
